_readme: In-app path literals in CareBase client source that check-frontend-route-links.mjs must not
fail on.
WHY THIS GATE EXISTS. check-server-route-links.mjs enforces that every in-app path built in a
migration or an edge function matches a route declared in App.tsx. The client had the same
defect and no check. carebaseGlossary.ts still carries the note: `/app/compliance` is not a
route App.tsx registers -- these three sent the reader to the 404 page. check-server-route-links
verifies exactly this rule, but only for links built in migrations and edge functions; a
client-side registry like this one is outside its scope. Three dead links reached users, were
repaired by hand, and the gap was written down instead of closed. Nothing stopped the fourth:
Dashboard.tsx reported `route: "/app/dashboard"` to product telemetry for a page mounted at
`/app`, so every benchmark_viewed row named a route that does not exist.
THE EXPECTED USE OF THIS FILE is a literal that is never navigated to as written -- either a
PREFIX TO MATCH (fed to startsWith/routeMatches) or a CONCATENATION BASE (only ever used as
`${base}/${id}`). The check reads every string literal in client source, which is what lets it
see a path routed through a constant or a ternary; the cost is that neither of those shapes is
distinguishable from a destination by looking at the literal alone.
Every entry names the code that consumes it, because that is the claim being made and it is the
part that can rot. A concatenation base is exempt only for as long as nothing navigates to it
bare -- `/admin/incidents` is one guard (`canLinkToOrgLists`) away from being a real dead link
for platform admins, and this file would not notice if that guard were removed. Re-read the
consumer before trusting an entry.
It is NOT a place to excuse a link that is genuinely broken. Declare the route or correct the
link instead.

/account.reason: A prefix to match, not a destination. `productModules.ts` uses it in INTERNAL_APP_PREFIXES, which productModuleForPath() feeds to matchesPath() to decide whether a path is inside the app shell at all before any module gate is consulted. The routes underneath it are real and declared (/account/security, /account/notifications, /account/announcements, /account/whats-new, /account/manager-digest/:id); bare /account is deliberately not one of them.

/app/regulatory.reason: A prefix to match, not a destination. `helpCopilot.ts` lists it in the compliance_risk intent's routePrefixes, which routeMatches() tests against the user's current location to pick which help answer applies. It is intentionally the shared stem of /app/regulatory-crosswalk and /app/regulatory-copilot -- both declared routes -- so that either page resolves to the same intent. Nothing navigates to /app/regulatory.

/admin/incidents.reason: A concatenation base for the platform-admin incident detail route, which IS declared (/admin/incidents/:id). No /admin/incidents list route exists. Alerts.tsx builds `${incidentDetailBase}/${alert.linked_incident_id}`. FacilityDetail.tsx also has a bare `${incidentsBasePath}?facility=…` link, but it renders inside `canLinkToOrgLists`, which is `user?.role !== "platform_admin"` -- so the branch that would produce this literal never renders it. Remove that guard and this becomes a real 404 for platform admins.
/admin/incidents.consumed_by: incidentDetailBase in pages/app/Alerts.tsx; incidentsBasePath in pages/app/FacilityDetail.tsx (bare use guarded by canLinkToOrgLists)

/admin/inspections.reason: A concatenation base for the platform-admin inspection-item detail route, which IS declared (/admin/inspections/:id). No /admin/inspections list route exists. Only used as `${inspectionDetailBase}/${alert.linked_inspection_item_id}`.

/admin/residents.reason: A concatenation base for the platform-admin resident routes, which ARE declared (/admin/residents/:id and /admin/residents/:residentId/assessment-forms/:formId). ResidentDetail.tsx states the rule in its own comment: "There is no /admin/residents list route; keep nested links working, but return 'Back' to a valid origin." Every use appends a segment.
/admin/residents.consumed_by: residentsBasePath in components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx; residentPathPrefix in pages/app/IncidentDetail.tsx, ResidentDetail.tsx, ResidentAssessmentFormEditor.tsx and the resident-tabs

/passport.reason: A `cleanPath` in PUBLIC_ACCESS_FLOWS, not a destination. A cleanPath is only navigated to when consumePublicAccessToken() rewrites the URL to hide a secret token, and that function requires a storageKey. The training-passport flow has `storageKey: null` -- its slug is public content identity, not a credential -- so nothing ever strips it and nothing lands on bare /passport. routeRegistration.test.ts encodes the same distinction: it asserts registration only for `PUBLIC_ACCESS_FLOWS.filter((flow) => flow.storageKey)`. The route users reach, /passport/:slug, is declared.
/passport.consumed_by: PUBLIC_ACCESS_FLOWS in lib/publicAccessToken.ts; registration asserted for storage-backed flows only in lib/routeRegistration.test.ts

/verify.reason: Same as /passport: a `cleanPath` for the certificate-verification flow, which also has `storageKey: null`, so consumePublicAccessToken() never rewrites to it. /verify/:slug is declared.

/app/help/tickets.reason: A concatenation base for the support-ticket detail route, which IS declared (/app/help/tickets/:id). No bare /app/help/tickets list route exists -- the list lives at /app/help. Only used as `${admin ? "/admin/support-tickets" : "/app/help/tickets"}/${entityId}`.
